literal: Misery many causing, prosperity destroying, than gambling, poverty bringing one thing is not.
translation: There is nothing else that brings such utter poverty as gambling, which inflicts many miseries and ruins one's prosperity.
modern: பல துன்பங்களை உண்டாக்கி, சிறப்பையும் செல்வத்தையும் அழிக்கும் சூதாட்டத்தைப் போல, வறுமையைத் தரும் வேறு ஒரு செயல் இல்லை.
explanation: This couplet warns against the destructive nature of gambling. It explains that gambling inflicts multiple miseries (ciṟumai) upon a person and completely ruins their wealth and social standing (cīr). The poet emphasizes that there is absolutely no other vice or misfortune (oṉṟu il) that drags a person into such deep destitution (vaṟumai) as gambling does. The word 'cīr' is crucial here, representing both material prosperity and the honor or reputation that a person loses when they gamble.
